## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rājovādajātaka* (Ja 151) is a narrative in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, set at Jetavana and framed as an instruction on royal virtue (*rājovāda*) delivered to a king [Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is reborn as King Brahmadatta of Benares, who rules with such justice that litigation ceases throughout the realm [Fausböll 1879; Söhnen-Thieme]. Seeking to discover any hidden flaws in his conduct, Brahmadatta travels through the kingdom incognito [Söhnen-Thieme]. In a narrow carriage-pass where two chariots cannot pass each other, his carriage encounters that of King Mallika of Kosala [Fausböll 1879; Söhnen-Thieme]. Determining who should yield the right of way, their respective charioteers describe the moral character of their rulers [Fausböll 1879]. While Mallika rules by returning "roughness for the rough" (*daḷhaṁ daḷhassa*) and goodness for goodness, Brahmadatta conquers anger with non-anger, wickedness with goodness, meanness with generosity, and untruth with truth; recognizing the superior virtue of non-retaliatory righteousness, Mallika yields the way [Fausböll 1879; Barua 1921; Goh; Söhnen-Thieme]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), Mallika's charioteer is identified as Moggallāna, King Mallika as Ānanda, Brahmadatta's charioteer as Sāriputta, and Brahmadatta as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1879].

 Furthermore, the motif and verses of the moral contest between the two kings are shared with the northern recension of the *Mahābhārata* (MBh 5.39.58) [Söhnen-Thieme]. DharmaNexus records textual reuse within Pali literature, identifying matching segments in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
